newsitem.title: USA: Stock falls amid disputed claims by Bear Stearns.
newsitem.headline: Stock falls amid disputed claims by Bear Stearns.

text.p: The stock of U.S. Diagnostic Inc. tumbled Monday in heavy trading amid claims, disputed by the company, that a key executive was a convicted criminal.
The company said the man was only a consultant.
The stock fell as low as $7.875 on Nasdaq before closing down $2.6875 at $8.375. It was the fifth most-active stock on the exchange, with almost 4.2 million shares changing hands.

Bear, Stearns & Co., which began following the company on Dec. 9 with a buy recommendation, suddenly ended its coverage Monday, saying it had learned that Keith Greenberg pleaded guilty to fraud and conspiracy in 1994.

U.S. Diagnostic, which operates a chain of medical diagnostic centres, had described Greenberg as a "co-founder of (the company) and a member of the management team," Bear Stearns analysts A.J. Rice and Tom Gallucci said in a research note.
Greenberg pleaded guilty in September 1994 in federal court in New York to fraud and conspiracy to defraud the United States, Bear Stearns said.
U.S. Diagnostic President Joseph Paul in an interview confirmed Greenberg's record, but argued that he was never a company officer or director, only a consultant.

Paul also said Bear Stearns had a "vendetta" against U.S. Diagnostic for hiring Smith Barney last week as lead manager of future security offerings by the company, which changed its name from U.S. Diagnostic Labs Inc. in October.
Bear Stearns officials were not immediately available. Calls to Rice and Gallucci for comment were not returned.

"We have learned information regarding the prior experiences and background of an individual associated with U.S. Diagnostic Inc. that causes us to lose confidence in our ability to assess ongoing developments at the company," Rice and Gallucci wrote.
Paul said Greenberg had never been an officer or director of the company and all public filings were "correct in all material aspects."
"He (Greenberg) was always an outside consultant," he said.
Regarding the analysts' claims that Greenberg was a co-founder of the company, Paul said Greenberg was among a group of parties that received shares soon after the company was created in 1993.

"I started the company in June 1993, and some of my founding shares were given to several people for helping me. He was one of them because he worked for the firm that fiananced our first bridge loan," Paul said.
"What A.J. (Rice) did was that he chose to pick out some information without looking at the issue ... because we signed a letter of engagement with Smith Barney and not them," Paul said.
He said that under a five-year contract, Greenberg's consulting company seeks acquisitions for U.S. Diagnostic.
Greenberg is paid only for deals that are consummated, Paul said.
